title: His Letters Now Follow His Real Class, Not a Clock | vitalii.no
description:
A kid's letter-learning app was teaching him letters his own class hadn't reached yet — because it ran on a calendar, not on the classroom.

The practice app assumed two new letters every week, counting from the first day of school. But the real grade-1 class started letters in week forty-two, and in its own order — not the alphabet, not the app's assumption. By November the gap between what the app quizzed and what the class had actually taught had quietly grown to about fifteen letters.

A new refreshSchoolLetters() function, running inside a lightweight Cloudflare Workers cron job that already ticks every 15 minutes, now scans each child's weekly class-plan text for the real letter-teaching goal line and publishes the parsed, ordered list to a small settings record — never the plan text itself. A letterPlan() helper in the app then computes exactly which letters the class has covered up to the current week, falling back to the old fixed clock only when no real plan exists yet.

The known-letters list now matches the exact letters the class has covered, closing the roughly 15-letter gap that had built up by November.
